page: Amazon Web Services c8gn.48xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro System and driven by the AWS ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 processor family. The server provides 192 dedicated physical cores and 192 vCPUs at a 1.0 thread-per-core ratio operating at 2.7 GHz, eliminating hyperthreading contention. Cache configuration includes 64 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 36 MB of L3 cache. Memory capacity totals 384.0 GB, establishing a compute-focused ratio of 2.0 GB of memory per core. The instance includes no discrete GPUs and provides no local instance storage, requiring workloads to rely on remote storage solutions such as Amazon EBS.

Benchmark results demonstrate significant multi-core scalability and memory throughput. The system reaches top-tier percentiles in multi-threaded decompression, Clang software compilation, ray tracing, and stress-ng multi-core evaluations. Large-block memory read bandwidth reaches 959.79 GB/sec, while write operations achieve 435.96 GB/sec. In-memory operations also show high efficiency, recording 381.9 million operations per second in Redis SET benchmarks. In contrast to its parallel throughput, single-core performance ranks within the middle 50% across Geekbench and stress-ng tests, indicating that processing gains are derived from massive parallelism rather than individual core clock frequencies.

Network performance is a primary feature of the configuration, supporting a baseline bandwidth of 600 Gbps. This substantial network interface compensates for the lack of local disks by facilitating fast access to network-attached storage and low-latency inter-node communication. From a resource-density perspective, the arm64 Neoverse-V2 design delivers efficient throughput per core for distributed tasks. The c8gn.48xlarge is suited for network-intensive and parallel processing workloads, including large-scale software compilation, Redis in-memory caches, high-throughput static web serving, and distributed batch computing architectures.
description: Amazon Web Services c8gn.48xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the Nitro hypervisor and powered by 192 dedicated AWS ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 cores operating at 2.7 GHz with a 1:1 physical-to-virtual core ratio. The platform integrates 384.0 GB of system memory, providing 2.0 GB per core, and delivers a baseline network bandwidth of 600 Gbps. It contains zero local storage drives and includes no hardware GPUs, necessitating network-attached storage architectures. Benchmark data highlights top-tier multi-threaded processing, evidenced by high throughput in stress-ng multi-core testing, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, Clang software compilation, and ray tracing. Memory throughput is similarly top-tier, sustaining 959.79 GB/sec in large-block read operations. However, single-core execution speeds in Geekbench and stress-ng remain average. The hardware configuration delivers high resource density and qualitative cost efficiency for highly parallel, network-heavy applications, making it well matched for distributed compilation pipelines, static web serving clusters, large-scale Redis in-memory deployments, and intensive parallel computing.
